question: Does the public bus transport operator actually considers environmental sustainability in planning and delivering urban transport services and investments?
step2_answer: ANSWER: Yes, BMTC acts on environmental sustainability through specific operational measures, but it has no comprehensive framework covering all its functions. The evidence fits the 2.5 band (explicit recognition with isolated measures), not 5. | EVIDENCE: (1) BMTC Annual Administration Report 2024-25 (BMTC-46), Ch. 13 Environment: an Environment Cell has existed since 2003. The Environmental Policy is limited to broad commitments, e.g. 'Adopt environment friendly transport operations through technological up-gradation and pollution reduction measures on continual basis'. Measures listed: 1369 electric buses and 1643 BS-VI diesel buses in operation at March 2025; 709 aged buses scrapped in 2024-25; water recycling plants in 45 depots (95% recovery); rainwater harvesting; solar roof-top PV at bus stations and TTMCs; monthly emission testing at depots; smoke-check drives with KSPCB. (2) The same report states 2025-26 plans: 'it is planned to induct 148 Non AC & 262 AC and totally 410 Electric Buses on GCC Model. Further, it is planned to scrap 707 diesel old buses.' It also sets a diesel efficiency target ('Planned to achieve HSD KMPL of 3.77'). (3) CAG Performance Audit (BMTC-77, covering 2017-18 to 2021-22): 'Though BMTC did not have any comprehensive environmental policy, There were certain initiatives such as scrapping of old vehicles and adoption of electric buses in the fleet and rainwater harvesting'.
